note: Ataxia, peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy, and hypotonia are well-documented core features of FDXR deficiency, though reported literature rates for ataxia (43%) and neuropathy (23%) in reviewed cohorts suggest 70-85% may be an overestimate.

evidence.text: A literature review of 44 reported patients with FDXR mutations revealed an incidence of sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy in 22.72% and ataxia in 43.18%, with hypotonia and pyramidal signs also frequently observed.

source.title: FDXR-associated disease: a challenging differential diagnosis with inflammatory peripheral neuropathy
source.quote: The review of clinical findings in previously described cases from literature reveals also a significant incidence of sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy (22.72%) and ataxia (43.18%). To date, 44 patients with FDXR mutations have been reported.

evidence.text: FDXR deficiency exhibits a broad spectrum of neurological features, including hypotonia, spasticity, ataxia, and movement disorders alongside optic atrophy and acoustic neuropathy.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and genetic spectrum of FDXR deficiency by functional validation of variants of uncertain significance
source.quote: such as hypotonia, spasticity, ataxia, movement disorders, … and phenotypic data of over 30 patients with FDXR deficiency… occurring phenotypes of optic atrophy, acoustic neuropathy
